tldr_label: TL;DR — Americans vote as US strikes hit an Iranian island and oil swings on hopes of peace

tldr_bullets.label: US vote
tldr_bullets.body: Control of Congress and 36 governorships is on the ballot. The first polls close at 6 p.m. ET, and Fox News rates the Senate a toss-up. [[TAG:info:polls close 6pm ET]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: US officials say they carried out 'defensive' strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island on the eve of the vote. Vance says talks have made progress, while officials say Netanyahu is pressing for a wider attack after the midterms. [[TAG:danger:US strikes]]

tldr_bullets.label: Oil
tldr_bullets.body: Brent fell about 7.6% to $104.77 on Monday on hopes of a deal, then edged up in Asia after reports of the strikes.

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The S&P 500 fell for a third straight day. Apple and Palantir beat estimates but slid after hours on their outlooks.

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Ukrainian officials say Russian bombs on an aid center in Zaporizhzhia region killed at least 24 people, with some reports saying 26. [[TAG:danger:24+ killed]]

tldr_bullets.label: Europe
tldr_bullets.body: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever offered to resign over the budget, and Poland's fight over its top court deepened.

sections.title: America Votes
sections.summary: Congress and 36 governorships are on the line; the first polls close at 6 p.m. ET

paragraphs.heading: What's at stake
paragraphs.body: Fox News said voters decide control of the House and Senate, where Republicans hold 53 seats, as well as governor's races in 36 states, and it rated the Senate a toss-up. ABC News (Australia) said polls point to close races. Georgia and Mississippi hold runoffs if no candidate wins a majority. [[TAG:warning:close races]]

paragraphs.heading: When results come
paragraphs.body: Fox News' guide says the first polls close at 6 p.m. ET in parts of Kentucky and Indiana and the last at 1 a.m. ET. Decision Desk HQ's hour-by-hour guide lists bellwether counties to watch, and PBS listed closing times for the battleground states.

sections.title: Strikes and Signals on Iran
sections.summary: US strikes Qeshm Island as Vance cites progress and Netanyahu presses for a wider attack

paragraphs.heading: Qeshm strikes
paragraphs.body: ABC News and CNN reported that US officials described strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island as defensive, carried out after Iranian fire at a US aircraft, and not a return to major combat. The National said Iranian state media reported explosions on the island. The reports rely on anonymous officials, and the damage has not been independently confirmed. [[TAG:danger:US strikes]]

paragraphs.heading: Talks and pressure
paragraphs.body: CBS News reported that Trump says a peace deal is still possible. PBS said Iran's delegation left the talks in Qatar after a tense weekend. Al Jazeera reported that Tehran is pushing a faster plan to reopen Hormuz in return for an end to the blockade and sanctions. AP, via Spectrum News, reported that officials say Netanyahu is pressing Trump to attack Iran after the midterms. Axios described their phone call as frank. [[TAG:warning:mixed signals]]

sections.sources: ABC News, CNN, The National, CBS News, PBS NewsHour, Al Jazeera, Spectrum News/AP, Axios

sections.title: Markets
sections.summary: Oil plunges on hopes of peace; Apple and Palantir beat estimates but fall after hours

paragraphs.heading: Oil
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that crude sold off more than 7% on hopes of peace talks with Iran, with Brent settling at $104.77. Oilprice.com tied the drop to a circulating draft proposal to end the war. CNBC later reported that oil rose in early Asian trade after reports of the US strike on Qeshm. [[TAG:warning:oil volatile]]

paragraphs.heading: Stocks
paragraphs.body: Yahoo Finance's index tally showed the S&P 500 down 0.51% to 7,541.40, its third loss in a row, and the Nasdaq down about 1.1%, while the Dow rose 0.41%. StockTitan said tech pulled the Nasdaq lower as oil tumbled.

paragraphs.heading: Apple and Palantir
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Apple and Palantir both fell after hours. Investinglive said both beat estimates, with Apple dragged down by its margin guidance and Palantir by slowing contract growth. Reported after-hours moves range from about 2% to 3%.

sections.title: Israel's Opposition Lines Up
sections.summary: All four opposition leaders back Eisenkot as Herzog starts with the smallest parties

paragraphs.heading: Backing Eisenkot
paragraphs.body: Ynet reported that support for Eisenkot is growing, putting pressure on undecided parties. Saudi Gazette said Israeli opposition parties are backing him to form a government, after Avigdor Liberman and Yair Golan joined Naftali Bennett. The Jerusalem Post reported earlier that the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend him.

paragraphs.heading: Process
paragraphs.body: The Jerusalem Post reported that Herzog will open consultations on Wednesday with the smallest parties first, an unusual order. In a separate analysis it said the haredi parties hold the key to any government. The Knesset is due to be sworn in on November 10. [[TAG:info:talks Wednesday]]

sections.title: Ukraine
sections.summary: Russian bombs on a school used as an aid center kill at least 24 in Zaporizhzhia region

paragraphs.heading: Komyshuvakha
paragraphs.body: The Kyiv Independent, citing Ukraine's emergency service, reported that Russian bombs hit a school used as a humanitarian aid center in Komyshuvakha and killed 24 people, including rescuers and police. Russia then struck a shelter where people had taken refuge. The Korea Times and Al Jazeera put the toll at 26. Zelensky called it an 'exceptionally horrific strike'. [[TAG:danger:24 to 26 killed]]

paragraphs.heading: Talks
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that Ukrainian and US officials are arranging working-level talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi, with the US mediating. Zelensky warned that Ukrainian intelligence expects a large Russian attack on energy networks timed to the US vote.

sections.sources: Kyiv Independent, Korea Times, Al Jazeera

sections.title: Europe
sections.summary: Belgium's prime minister offers to quit over the budget; Poland's court fight deepens

paragraphs.heading: Belgium
paragraphs.body: France 24 and ABC News reported that Prime Minister Bart De Wever offered his resignation after his five-party coalition failed to agree a 2027 budget, and that King Philippe is weighing whether to accept it. The government is trying to cut a deficit above 5% of GDP. [[TAG:warning:government crisis]]

paragraphs.heading: Poland
paragraphs.body: Euronews reported that the Constitutional Tribunal crisis between Prime Minister Donald Tusk and President Karol Nawrocki has 'exploded'. Tusk urged Nawrocki to recognize judges elected by parliament. Plataforma Media explained the dispute over who runs the court after a judge whose authority Nawrocki disputes suspended the court's president. Accounts of the late-night standoff at the court differ by outlet.

sections.sources: France 24, ABC News, Euronews, Plataforma Media

sections.summary: South Africa and Rwanda lose duty-free US trade access; Ebola deaths keep climbing

paragraphs.body: Moneyweb reported that South Africa and Rwanda lost duty-free access to the US under the African Growth and Opportunity Act after Washington found they failed its eligibility criteria. [[TAG:warning:AGOA suspended]]

paragraphs.body: Africanews put the DR Congo Ebola death toll at 5,372, with a fatality rate above 50%. NBC News reported more than 10,000 cases. Figures vary by source and reporting date. [[TAG:danger:5,300+ deaths]]
